I can’t help but notice that this flood resembles a hydroelectric dam failure which also has me wondering if this was an intentional dam failure meant  to displace these communities in order to continue developing more hydroelectric dams up that river without opposition or push back.

I don’t trust MSM or their so called “experts” since COVID especially when they all seem to be reading from the same script within an hour this disaster.

If a hydroelectric damn failed intentionally or via a catastrophic engineering error, someone needs to be held accountable!!

A flash flood doesn’t make sense considering there was no rain in that area for two days and ice coming off the mountain wouldn’t create that much water and there would be a clear satellite imagine available if this was caused by a glacier breaking off the mountain. 

Something isn’t adding up here!!  An avalanche here in Canada doesn’t create a flash flood. 🤦‍♀️

replies.author: @chaselandtv
replies.text:
I can understand why an event like this would raise a lot of questions, especially when the available information feels incomplete. Disasters involving glaciers, rivers, landslides, and hydropower infrastructure can be extremely complex, and early reports are not always enough to establish exactly what happened.

At the same time, we’d be careful about assuming an intentional dam failure without solid evidence. If there was an engineering failure, negligence, or any other preventable cause, then a transparent investigation and accountability would absolutely be important. Hopefully the technical findings will make the sequence of events much clearer.
